title: Photo Exit Bundle
user: Families leaving or reducing reliance on Google Photos who need a usable local photo archive without losing albums, dates, motion companions, or a simple way to share with mixed-device relatives.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A Pixel-owning parent has outgrown Google storage, worries about account lockout, and explicitly wishes for an easy way to back up Google Photos.
The request notes that Google Photos and Drive behavior differ and that a 300k-photo collection makes manual migration impractical (37 reactions, 171 comments).

recurrence: Account-lockout anxiety, growing family libraries, and storage bills turn this into a recurring exit problem; the rclone thread's long discussion shows the integration is persistently awkward.
current_workaround: Download Takeout ZIPs, use rclone scripts, switch to another cloud, or self-host Immich/PhotoPrism and manually repair metadata.
incumbents_and_gap: Google Takeout exports data and rclone copies files; Immich and PhotoPrism host libraries. The missing middle is a local, explainable migration report that identifies what survived and what needs user attention.
smallest_useful_product: A local Takeout-to-folder converter that pairs JSON metadata and motion-video files, recreates dated folders/album manifests, produces a duplicate and missing-companion report, and writes a portable README. Non-goals: Google API scraping, hosted galleries, or face recognition.
success_measure: At least 80% of pilot exports finish with fewer than 1% unclassified assets and users open the resulting archive on a second machine.
monetization: one-time — it is a finite migration with no credible reason to retain family photos.
constraints: Runs entirely on user-selected files; do not claim full fidelity for unsupported Google metadata; preserve originals; comply with Google Takeout formats and avoid account automation.
why_distinct: This is an exit-quality checker and portable archive builder, not a Google Photos clone or another sync daemon.
